chunks: Ibn Nuh said: The first person to narrate this epistle to us was Abu al-Husayn Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Tamam,

and mentioned that he had copied it from the back of the manuscript (daraj) that was in the possession of Abu al-Hasan ibn Dawood. When Abu al-Hasan ibn Dawood arrived, I read it to him, and he mentioned that this very manuscript was sent by the people of Qom to the Sheikh Abu al-Qasim, containing various questions, to which he replied on its back in the handwriting of Ahmad ibn Ibrahim al-Nuwaybakhti, and this manuscript remained with Abu al-Hasan ibn Dawood.

key_terms.التَّوْقِيع: Epistle or letter from the Imam
key_terms.الدَّرَج: Manuscript or document, specifically referring to the famous 'Daraj' document
key_terms.الشَّيْخُ أَبُو الْقَاسِمِ: The Sheikh Abu al-Qasim (Husayn ibn Rauh)

ai.seo_question: How was the epistle of the Imam transmitted and preserved in the manuscript known as the Daraj?
ai.summary: This narration highlights the meticulous chain of transmission (isnad) used to authenticate the Imam's written decrees, tracing the epistle from the people of Qom to the Special Emissary Abu al-Qasim Husayn ibn Rauh, and finally to the scholarly elite like Ahmad ibn Ibrahim al-Nuwaybakhti. It underscores the role of the 'Daraj' (manuscript folder) as a primary vehicle for preserving the Imam's direct responses to community inquiries during the Minor Occultation, ensuring the continuity of religious authority and legal guidance.

en.sayyid-athar-husain-s-h-rizvi: Ibn Nuh has said that first of all Abul Husain Muhammad bin Ali bin Tamam has narrated that he quoted this epistle from the manuscript that was in the possession of Abul Hasan bin Dawood

and when he came, I read out that copy to him and he also said that the same copy was sent by the people of Qom to Husain bin Rauh and its reply arrived written on its back by Ahmad bin Ibrahim Naubakhti and this copy was obtained from Abul Husain bin Dawood.
